clue.text: Proved difficult to conceal stink with instrumental 21ing device?

indicators.note: to conceal something is to hide it inside, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: proved difficult means was hard
BO is body odour, a stink

explanation.surface: Someone struggling to hide a bad smell while playing some musical cleaning gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is CLEAN, so '21ing' reads 'cleaning'. 'to conceal' puts BO inside WAS HARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A washboard is a ribbed board for scrubbing clothes, also played as a percussion instrument in skiffle bands.

clue.text: Bird call heard in New York diner?

indicators.note: the word is said in a New York accent, as it would be shouted across a diner, softening the T

parts.note: the call a customer makes in a diner is for the waiter

explanation.surface: A birdsong picked up by someone eating in a Manhattan diner.
explanation.walkthrough: In a New York accent the T in the call for service is flapped, so it comes out like a long-legged bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A wader is any long-legged bird that feeds in shallow water, such as a heron or curlew.

clue.text: Persuaded to keep strong supporting character created by Dickens's pen

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: persuaded, as of a customer won over, means sold

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting piece sits underneath, so it follows the other

parts.note: Uriah Heep is the scheming clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield
f, forte, is the musical abbreviation for loud or strong

explanation.surface: A tale of a powerful figure written with the novelist's own pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like Dickens's writing tool; it is an enclosure for animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheepfold is an enclosure for sheep, and a pen is any such animal enclosure.

parts.note: read not as a security matter but as a moment when one's hair, or locks, looks so awful it needs restyling

explanation.definitionFit: A bad hair day is a day when one's hair is unmanageable, and by extension a day of things going wrong.

clue.text: Don't vote with a black mark

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a stain is a mark

explanation.surface: Refusing to cast a ballot because of a blot on one's record.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to decline to cast a vote, which is what an instruction not to vote asks.

parts.note: read as a man's name belonging to the Isle of Man: the island's capital town shares its name with a common male first name

explanation.definitionFit: Douglas is the capital of the Isle of Man and also a common man's first name.

parts.note: OS, outsize, is the clothing abbreviation for very large
aka, also known as, introduces an alias

explanation.surface: A Japanese city's huge pseudonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Osaka is a major port city on the Japanese island of Honshu.

indicators.note: speeches are spoken words, so the word for permitted is taken as it sounds when said

parts.note: permitted means allowed

explanation.surface: Speech-making is allowed, as was said.
explanation.definitionFit: Something read aloud is said so as to be heard, that is, voiced rather than silent.

clue.text: Channel broken up by weak battery

indicators.note: one word is split open so that another fills the gap

parts.note: an artery is a channel, as a main road or blood vessel
ill means sickly, weak

explanation.surface: A TV channel interrupted because its power supply is flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battery' looks like a power cell; it is a battery of guns.
explanation.definitionFit: A battery is a unit of big guns, and artillery is heavy guns collectively.

indicators.note: one piece enters, coming into, the other

parts.note: the late means dead, as in the late king
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: Worry about resistance arriving late in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is great fear or apprehension, a direct synonym.

parts.note: a gravy train is easy money, but here the gravy travels by another vessel, a jug-like boat for sauce

explanation.definitionFit: A sauceboat is a boat-shaped jug for serving gravy or sauce at table.

parts.note: 21 is CLEAN: a clean joke can be retold anywhere, and the word itself is printed twice, said over again

explanation.walkthrough: 21 is CLEAN; inoffensive material is fit to be told again in polite company.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repeatable is fit to be said again, as an inoffensive joke is.

indicators.note: 7 down is ALOUD, so the next word is taken as it sounds

parts.note: 20 and 6 down together are TICK OVER, which means idle, as an engine does

explanation.surface: An engine idling, said out loud, and someone calling a loved one sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: Cross-references: 20/6 is TICK OVER, and 7 is ALOUD, the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A darling, such as a pop star adored by fans, is an idol.

clue.text: Silly old bugger, he's the father of his namesake

indicators.note: silly suggests letters behaving foolishly, so they are rearranged

parts.note: contracted he is; the apostrophe adds no letter

explanation.surface: An insult hurled at a foolish old man who has a son named after him.
explanation.walkthrough: The father, the 41st US president, shares his name with his son, the 43rd.
explanation.definitionFit: The elder US president of that name was father to the later president who shares his name.

clue.text: Scotsman's beginning half his breakfast with an item of his?

indicators.note: the beginning of the word Scotsman's is its first letter
half of the breakfast word is its first four letters

parts.note: the Scotsman's traditional breakfast is porridge

explanation.surface: A Scot starts on his porridge, with the clue asking what he might wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his' points back to the Scotsman: the pouch worn at the front of a kilt.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporran is the pouch worn over a kilt, an item of a Scotsman's dress.

clue.text: Jaguar, perhaps, gets to display evidence of fight

parts.note: to sport something is to wear or display it
a scar is left by a wound from a fight

explanation.surface: A big cat shows the wounds of a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jaguar' looks like the big cat; it is the car make.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jaguar is an example of a fast two-seat car built for performance.

clue.text: Spirit with which a certain Graf covering court runs

indicators.note: one piece covers the other by wrapping around it

parts.note: Graf Spee was a German admiral, best known through the battleship named after him
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A ghost accompanying Steffi Graf as she races round a tennis court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Graf' calls up the tennis player; the Graf here is Admiral Graf Spee.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectre is a ghost or apparition, a spirit of the dead.

indicators.note: blurring makes the outlines of these letters indistinct, mixing them up

explanation.surface: A photography method that leaves pale objects smudged.
explanation.definitionFit: Time-lapse photography shoots frames at long intervals to show slow change sped up.

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: LAB for Labour and DO for party, each said with a stammer on its first letter: L-LAB D-DO

explanation.surface: A political party with a stammer comes back as an outcast.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddball is an eccentric person who does not fit in, a misfit.

clue.text: Domestic god puts on some bits of bacon

parts.note: a lar is a Roman household god
to don clothes is to put them on

explanation.surface: A god of the home dresses up in rashers.
explanation.definitionFit: Lardons are small strips or cubes of bacon used in cooking.

clue.text: Start to scoff duff that's delicious

indicators.note: the start of the word scoff is its first letter

parts.note: duff, British slang, means poor or useless, as does crummy

explanation.surface: Wolfing down a pudding that tastes great.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duff' suggests the pudding (plum duff); here it means bad, useless.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrummy is informal British for scrumptious, meaning delicious.

parts.note: a mouse goes squeak, and the cartoon character's public reputation is wholesome and spotless

explanation.definitionFit: Squeaky-clean means utterly wholesome or above reproach, apt for a mouse's spotless reputation.

parts.note: a tick is a moment, a second
in cricket an over is six balls bowled

explanation.surface: In cricket, a second over goes along without incident.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six deliveries in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine that ticks over runs steadily at low speed, so things proceed smoothly.

clue.text: Doctor Roger let us put a pin in it

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A request to a medic named Roger to let them insert a pin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pin' is slang for a leg, which is what goes into this garment part.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin is slang for a leg, and a trouser leg is what one puts a leg into.

clue.text: Rival of younger 13 retaining second 13's surname?

indicators.note: retaining means holding on to, so one piece stays inside the other

parts.note: Al Gore ran against the younger George Bush in the 2000 election

explanation.surface: Asking whether the president's opponent, holding a second, gives the president's family name.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is GEORGE BUSH; his surname is a bush, and this is a prickly yellow-flowered one.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorse is a spiny shrub, so it is a bush, the president's surname.

indicators.note: off means not right, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: 1m read as one M

explanation.surface: A signpost reading one mile away.
explanation.walkthrough: '1m' looks like a distance; spell it out as ONE M and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a sign of what is to come, a portent.

clue.text: Drink a lot in closing bars?

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other

parts.note: a coda is the closing passage of a piece of music
reams means a lot, a great quantity

explanation.surface: Drinking heavily in pubs at closing time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' look like pubs; they are bars of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Cream soda is a sweet vanilla-flavoured fizzy drink.

clue.text: Meal (having missed starter) that is superior to sole

indicators.note: missing its starter means the first letter of the meal word is dropped

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: A diner who skipped the first course is still above the fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sole' looks like the fish on a menu; it is the bottom of a shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper of a shoe is the part above the sole.

indicators.note: of here means taken from within, so the answer comes out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: An accidental car crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-in is a clash or confrontation, and literally a collision.

parts.note: the word fetter sounds like feta, a cheese: so it is a cheese said aloud, as an instruction to say a cheese would produce

explanation.surface: Hinting at a shackle while telling someone to grin.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer read as an instruction, say a cheese, gives FETA, which sounds like 'fetter'.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographers tell their subjects to utter this phrase because it shapes the mouth into a grin.
